PocketSphinx 5.1.1
=====================

This is PocketSphinx, one of Carnegie Mellon University's open source large
vocabulary, speaker-independent continuous speech recognition engines.

Though the algorithms and models implemented by PocketSphinx are now
quite old (dating back to the 1970s in some cases!) they are still
useful in many applications due to their compactness and efficiency.

The version number is strangely large because there was a "release"
that people are using called 5prealpha, and we will use proper
[semantic versioning](https://semver.org/) from now on.

**Please see the LICENSE file for terms of use.**

Installation
------------

We now use CMake for building, which should give reasonable results
across Linux and Windows.  Not certain about Mac OS X because I don't
have one of those.  In addition, the audio library, which never really
built or worked correctly on any platform at all, has simply been
removed.

There is no longer any dependency on SphinxBase.  There is no
SphinxBase anymore.  This is not the SphinxBase you're looking for.
All your SphinxBase are belong to us.

There are some other dependencies that you may find useful in order to
use the example code (though they are not strictly necessary to build
and install).  On Debian GNU/Linux and its derivatives (such as
Raspberry Pi OS, Ubuntu, etc), you can install them with:

    sudo apt install \
        ffmpeg \
        libasound2-dev \
        libportaudio2 \
        libportaudiocpp0 \
        libpulse-dev \
        libsox-fmt-all \
        portaudio19-dev \
        sox

To install the Python module in a virtual environment (replace
`~/ve_pocketsphinx` with the virtual environment you wish to create),
from the top level directory:

```
python3 -m venv ~/ve_pocketsphinx
. ~/ve_pocketsphinx/bin/activate
pip install .
```

To install the C library and bindings (assuming you have access to
/usr/local - if not, use `-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX` to set a different
prefix in the first `cmake` command below):

```
cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build
cmake --build build --target install
```

Usage
-----

The `pocketsphinx` command-line program reads single-channel 16-bit
PCM audio from standard input or one or more files, and attempts to
recognize speech in it using the default acoustic and language model.
It accepts a large number of options which you probably don't care
about, a *command* which defaults to `live`, and one or more inputs
(except in `align` mode), or `-` to read f

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# ASR Bridge

将微信桌面端、微信输入法和豆包网页版语音识别整合成一个 Windows 应用及 OpenAI 兼容的本机音频转写接口。音频发送到所选后端的服务端，不发送给 OpenAI。

[English](README.en.md) · [MIT License](LICENSE) · [接口文档](docs/api.html) · [窗口版使用说明](docs/PORTABLE.md)

## 窗口版

使用与源码版本对应的 `WeChatASRBridge-0.3.1-windows-x64-portable.zip`，解压整个文件夹并运行 `WeChatASRBridge.exe`。本地构建产物在 `dist/`；GitHub Releases 的最新正式发布版本可能早于当前源码。

- **首页**：服务状态、三个独立并发池、Base URL、model 和接口文档入口。每个小格代表一个并发名额，占用显示绿色，空闲无填色。
- **手动转写**：选择 model、选择音频或示例音频、识别、复制或保存文字。
- **设置**：端口、本地 API Key 和三个后端各自的并发数。每个模型默认并发 4，可分别设置正整数；三个模型合计最多运行 8 个请求，超出本池或总额度的请求排队。首页显示总占用和各池占用。这些配置不是上游稳定性保证，旧版已保存的自定义值会保留。
- 关闭窗口后驻留托盘；正常退出会等待请求和原生会话清理。只停止本应用启动的服务。

![窗口版首页](docs/portable-preview.png)

## 模型路由

| model | 后端 | 条件 |
|---|---|---|
| `wechat-voice` | 微信桌面端 | 微信 4.1.13.65 已登录，账号的 iLink/Opus 能力可用 |
| `wetype-voice` | 微信输入法 | 已验证的微信输入法 3.0.0.34 正在运行 |
| `doubao-voice` | 豆包网页版匿名会话 | 能正常访问豆包网页及语音网关，无需浏览器登录 |

微信和输入法执行已适配模块的指纹核验，版本不匹配时拒绝原生调用；不需要同时满足所有后端的运行条件才能启动应用。某个后端不可用时，其他后端仍可使用。豆包使用普通游客初始化，不读取 Chrome/Edge 登录信息，也不保存浏览器 Cookie。

原生客户端与私有网页协议可能变化，当前实现不能保证任意版本或长期稳定运行。每池自定义值不会突破总计 8 路的运行上限，也不会提高上游限额。大并发池的格子分组显示，显示分页不会减少实际配置容量。

## 从源码运行

Windows x64，使用 Python 3.11 conda 环境：

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\setup.ps1
.\env\python.exe desktop.py
```

仅启动 HTTP 服务：

```powershell
.\env\python.exe server.py --port 8765 `
  --wechat-concurrency 4 --wetype-concurrency 4 --doubao-concurrency 4
```

也可使用 `start.ps1 -Background`；三个并发参数分别为 `-WechatConcurrency`、`-WetypeConcurrency`、`-DoubaoConcurrency`。停止使用 `stop.ps1 -Port 8765`。单后端诊断可使用 `server.py --backend wechat|wetype|doubao`；单后端同样使用对应的正式 model 名称。

## 接入其他程序

| 参数 | 值 |
|---|---|
| Base URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1` |
| model | 上表中的路由标识 |
| API Key | 未启用本地鉴权时任意值或留空均被忽略；启用后填设置中的密钥 |
| 转写 | `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions`，multipart 表单 |
| 模型列表 | `GET /v1/models` |
| 状态及并发池 | `GET /health`，只读，不提交识别 |
| HTML 接口文档 | `http://127.0.0.1:8765/docs`，也可离线打开 `docs/api.html` |

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:8765/v1", api_key="local",
                timeout=180, max_retries=0)
with open("audio.wav", "rb") as audio:
    result = client.audio.transcriptions.create(
        model="doubao-voice", file=audio, response_format="json")
print(result.text)
```

单个上传文件最大 25 MiB，完整解码后在内存中转写。支持 `json` 和 UTF-8 `text`；`stream=false`、`temperature=0` 仅作为兼容默认值。`language`、`prompt`、字幕、逐词时间戳、说话人分离及流式响应尚未实现，传入时明确返回错误。

# Claude Code Plugins Directory

A curated directory of high-quality plugins for Claude Code.

> **⚠️ Important:** Make sure you trust a plugin before installing, updating, or using it. Anthropic does not control what MCP servers, files, or other software are included in plugins and cannot verify that they will work as intended or that they won't change. See each plugin's homepage for more information.

## Structure

- **`/plugins`** - Internal plugins developed and maintained by Anthropic
- **`/external_plugins`** - Third-party plugins from partners and the community

## Installation

Plugins can be installed directly from this marketplace via Claude Code's plugin system.

To install, run `/plugin install {plugin-name}@claude-plugins-official`

or browse for the plugin in `/plugin > Discover`

## Contributing

### Internal Plugins

Internal plugins are developed by Anthropic team members. See `/plugins/example-plugin` for a reference implementation.

### External Plugins

Third-party partners can submit plugins for inclusion in the marketplace. External plugins must meet quality and security standards for approval. To submit a new plugin, use the [plugin directory submission form](https://clau.de/plugin-directory-submission).

## Plugin Structure

Each plugin follows a standard structure:

```
plugin-name/
├── .claude-plugin/
│   └── plugin.json      # Plugin metadata (required)
├── .mcp.json            # MCP server configuration (optional)
├── commands/            # Slash commands (optional)
├── agents/              # Agent definitions (optional)
├── skills/              # Skill definitions (optional)
└── README.md            # Documentation
```

## Plugin names are immutable

The `name` field in a marketplace entry is an **immutable slug**. Once a plugin has been published, its `name` must not change — users have it installed under that slug, and renaming it breaks their install with a `plugin-not-found` error.

- To change how a plugin is labeled in the UI, set or update `displayName` instead.
- If a rename is genuinely unavoidable, add an entry to the top-level `renames` map in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` so existing installs auto-migrate:

```json
"renames": {
  "old-name": "new-name"
}
```

The Claude Code plugin loader reads this map and transparently rewrites the old slug to the new one on the user's next sync.

candidates.readme_excerpt:
# earshot

**Ears for coding agents.**

<!-- launch video -->
[**Watch the 22 s launch film**](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/earshot/releases/tag/v0.1.0) - every sound in it was made
in code by `earshot forge`; no recordings, no music track.

![Frames from the launch film](docs/media/launch_frames.png)

AI coding agents can now write the code that renders a film, a product demo or a game. They still cannot hear what
they made. They cannot tell a premium key press from a cheap one, notice that a hit lands 80 ms after the cut, or
hear that the music swells in the wrong place.

earshot turns sound into evidence an agent can reason about: what a file sounds like in words, how well it fits a
description, the best moment inside a long recording, whether it is a real recording or code-synthesized, a
second-by-second listening transcript of a whole film, an annotated picture of it, and a scorecard against
professional launch films. It runs locally on CPU, as a CLI, a Python API and an MCP server.

With ears, an agent can also **make its own sounds in code** and improve them by listening (`earshot forge`, below).

```
$ earshot describe enter.ogg
  0.56 s short transient (attack 3 ms, decays in 190 ms). Sounds most like: a single mechanical keyboard key press
  (z +5.4), a soft key release click (z +3.6) ... [clear reading]. peak -0.1 dBFS, brightness 1.5 kHz ...

$ earshot match key.ogg "a deep thocky mechanical keyboard press" --alts "a clicky blue switch keyboard" "a mouse click"
  -> strong (z +3.7; would rank #2 among 322 vocabulary descriptions) ...

$ earshot find keys.ogg "a single mechanical key press" --top 4
  0:03.94-0:04.19 (0.24 s stroke, z +4.1 strong); 0:10.60-0:10.86 ...

$ earshot critique film.mp4
  VERDICT: close - 21 of 23 scored metrics in range ... FIX FIRST: 1. [major] nothing reaches body level until 0:01.01 ...
```

## What it does

| command | what an agent gets |
|---|---|
| `describe FILE` | what it sounds like: calibrated tags (z) with the closest alternative readings, AudioSet labels, measurements |
| `match FILE QUERY [--alts ...]` | how well a description fits: cosine, z among the vocabulary, a verdict (strong / plausible / weak / no match) with held-out evidence |
| `rank QUERY PATHS...` | many candidate files sorted by a description (pick the best download) |
| `find FILE QUERY` | the best moments inside a long recording, as sample trims (start / end seconds) |
| `compare FILE --refs DIR` / `ab A B` | nearest reference recordings an

candidates.description: The Open Framework for Building Agents
candidates.readme_excerpt:
eve

[eve](https://eve.dev/) is a filesystem-first framework for durable AI agents. Core agent capabilities live in conventional locations, so projects are easier to inspect, extend, and operate. ## The filesystem is the authoring interface A typical eve agent has this structure: ```text my-agent/ └── agent/ ├── agent.ts # Optional: model and runtime config ├── instructions.md # Required: the always-on system prompt ├── tools/ # Optional: typed functions the model can call │ └── get_weather.ts ├── skills/ # Optional: procedures loaded on demand │ └── plan_a_trip.md ├── channels/ # Optional: message channels (HTTP, Slack, Discord) │ └── slack.ts └── schedules/ # Optional: recurring cron jobs └── weekly_recap.ts ``` Read the [documentation](https://eve.dev/docs) for the full project layout and guides. ## Quick start ```bash npx eve@latest init my-agent ``` This creates a new `my-agent` directory, installs its dependencies, initializes Git, and starts the interactive terminal UI. The generated agent uses `openai/gpt-6-luna-fast` with high reasoning. To start with another AI Gateway model, pass its model ID: ```bash npx eve@latest init my-agent --model openai/gpt-5.6-terra ``` Passing `--model` without `--reasoning` uses the provider's default reasoning. Pass `--reasoning` to set it explicitly. To add eve to an existing project, pass a path: ```bash cd myapp npx eve@latest init . ``
